newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

President Suharto at the opening of the ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting stressed the need to focus on economic and not political matters at the inaugural ministerial meeting of World Trade Organisation (WTO). The WTO will meet in Singapore later this year.

Around 200 people gathered at Tanjung Priok in Jakarta to comemorate those who died in a 1984 battle with the police. An official file has never been opened on the incident in which the army opened fire on people protesting against the government. The army has said at least 18 people died in the incident but there have been recent calls for the National Commission on Human Rights to reopen the case.

Indonesia's logistics bureau (Bulog) chief Beddu Amang said the organisation's rice procurement in fiscal 1996/97 (April/March) will be around 1.4 million tonnes, down from forecasts of two million tonnes.

Indonesia will begin reducing tariffs on rice and sugar within the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) by 2003 ending the process in 2010. Previously Indonesia and the Philippines had suggested a 2020 deadline for the phasing out of tariffs on sensitive agricultural products.
